english: I don't necessarily think so.
tip: The 는 (neun) tucked into 생각하지는 않아요 (saenggakajineun anayo) makes the denial partial: with 꼭 (kkok = necessarily), it reads 'I don't necessarily think so', not a flat no.

english: I think this plan is good.
tip: ~다고 생각해요 = I think that ~: 좋다고 생각해요 (jotago saenggakaeyo).

english: I think that is correct.
tip: ~것 같아요 softens a claim: 맞는 것 같아요 (manneun geot gatayo) = seems right.

english: That opinion makes sense.
tip: 일리가 있다 = to have a point: 일리가 있어요 (illiga isseoyo).

english: I'm not certain, but it's probably so.
tip: -지는 않지만 (-jineun anchiman) = 'not exactly X, but': 확실하지는 않지만 (hwaksilhajineun anchiman) = I'm not certain, but... The 는 makes the denial partial.

english: I'll give it some thought.
tip: -아/어 볼게요 = I will try: 생각해 볼게요 (saenggakae bolgeyo).

target: 이 문제는 좀 더 고민해야 해요.
english: We need to think this over more.
tip: -아야 하다 = must: 고민해야 해요 (gominhaeya haeyo) = must ponder.

english: That depends on the situation.
tip: -에 따라 = depending on: 상황에 따라 (sanghwange ttara).

english: I don't think that's quite right.
tip: Koreans rarely say a flat no – 아닌 것 같아요 (anin geot gatayo) = 'it seems not so' turns disagreement into an impression, which is the polite default.

english: It's not that I oppose that opinion.
tip: -는 건 아니에요 (-neun geon anieyo) = 'it's not that I...': 반대하는 건 아니에요 (bandaehaneun geon anieyo) denies only the framing, not the whole idea.

english: It's because there isn't enough time.
tip: 왜냐하면 (waenyahamyeon) opens 'because' but can't end the sentence – it must close with -기 때문이에요: 부족하기 때문이에요 (bujokagi ttaemunieyo). Reason marked at both ends.

english: According to statistics, that isn't so.
tip: -에 따르면 = according to: 통계에 따르면 (tonggye-e ttareumyeon).

english: I'm speaking based on my experience.
tip: -을 근거로 = based on: 경험을 근거로 (gyeongheomeul geungeoro).

english: You shouldn't speak without grounds.
tip: -면 안 되다 = must not: 말하면 안 돼요 (malhamyeon an dwaeyo).

english: I worry AI might cut jobs.
tip: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 = worried that: 줄일까 봐 (juril-kka bwa).

english: It's hard to live without a smartphone.
tip: 없이는 = without: 스마트폰 없이는 (seumateupon eopsineun).

english: Exam-centered education is a problem.
tip: 위주 (wiju) = -centered: 시험 위주 = exam-focused.

english: The countryside is nicer to live in than the city.
tip: 살기 좋다 = good to live in: 살기 좋아요 (salgi joayo).

target: 가짜 뉴스가 사회에 나쁜 영향을 줘요.
english: Fake news has a bad influence on society.
tip: Influence is something you give in Korean: 영향을 줘요 (yeonghyangeul jwoyo) = literally 'gives influence'. Same with stress or help – 주다 (juda = give) does the work.

english: Don't trust ads too much.
tip: -지 마세요 (-ji maseyo) is the polite 'please don't': 믿지 마세요 (mitji maseyo) = please don't trust. It attaches to the bare verb stem, whatever the verb.

english: Still, I tend to be in favor.
tip: -는 편이다 = tend to: 찬성하는 편이에요 (chanseonghaneun pyeonieyo).

english: You can't necessarily say that's so.
tip: 꼭 (kkok = necessarily) plus a negative = 'not necessarily': 꼭 그렇다고 볼 수는 없어요 (kkok geureotago bol suneun eopseoyo) = you can't necessarily see it that way.

english: On reflection, I was wrong.
tip: -아 보니 = upon doing: 생각해 보니 (saenggakae boni) = now that I think.

english: Now that I hear it, it makes sense.
tip: -고 보니 = after doing: 듣고 보니 (deutgo boni).

english: We should lend an ear to opposing views too.
tip: 귀를 기울이다 (gwireul giurida) is literally 'tilt an ear' – leaning in to listen. 귀를 기울여야 해요 (gwireul giuryeoya haeyo) = we should lend an ear.

english: We should try to understand each other.
tip: -려고 (-ryeogo) marks purpose – 'in order to': 이해하려고 (ihaeharyeogo) = in order to understand. The goal comes before the trying, the reverse of English order.

target: 본 열차는 잠시 후 종착역인 부산역에 도착하겠습니다. 두고 내리시는 물건이 없도록 다시 한번 확인하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: This train will shortly arrive at its final stop, Busan Station. Please check once more that you have not left any belongings behind.
tip: -겠습니다 states a formal announced future: 도착하겠습니다 (dochakagetseumnida = will arrive).

target: 귀하께서 제출하신 지원 서류를 검토한 결과, 면접 대상자로 선정되셨음을 알려 드립니다.
english: Having reviewed the application documents you submitted, we are pleased to inform you that you have been selected for an interview.
tip: Formal notice ending -음을 알려 드립니다 (…eumeul allyeo deurimnida = we hereby inform you that…).

target: 지금부터 신랑 신부의 입장이 있겠습니다. 하객 여러분께서는 큰 박수로 맞아 주시기 바랍니다.
english: The bride and groom will now enter. Guests, please welcome them with a warm round of applause.
tip: -이/가 있겠습니다 announces an event formally: 입장이 있겠습니다 (ipjang-i itgetseumnida = there will be an entrance).

target: 삼가 고인의 명복을 빌며, 유가족 여러분께 깊은 위로의 말씀을 전합니다.
english: I humbly pray for the repose of the deceased and offer my deepest condolences to the bereaved family.
tip: 삼가 (samga = respectfully) opens formal condolences: 명복을 빕니다 (myeongbogeul bimnida = I pray for the repose).
